newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA OTC MARKET GOES INTO BUSINESS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA OTC MARKET GOES INTO BUSINESS.

text.p: A long-awaited over-the- counter (OTC) trading system intended to boost Romania's budding capital market went on line on Friday, trading shares of six companies, a system official said.

"Today's two-hour session, involving six companies and four securities companies, is a pilot phase, on which the organisation of future sessions will depend," RASDAQ system manager Mihai Catuneanu said.
Results of Friday's session will be released next week.

The RASDAQ system was developed on the model of the U.S. NASDAQ under a $21 million capital market project run by the U.S. Agency for International Development. It was officially inaugurated late last month and has been through tests since.

The six traded companies include a construction company, a medicine distributor, a jewellery making and marketing company and a plane engine maker. Shares of a railway building company and of a pig iron products manufacturer will also be traded.
The RASDAQ is expected eventually to trade 5,000 companies, most of them turned private in a mass selloff, with the help of 74 brokers and some 300 work stations across the country.
"We start with a handful of companies but more stocks will be in the market soon," said Mircea Ilie, general manager of the Romanian shareholders' registry.
Romania launched a mass privatisation a year ago in which 17 million Romanians could swap coupons for around 600 million shares in some 4,000 state companies.
Most brokers welcomed the start of the OTC system. "You are tempted to say it's funny to start with a few stocks and brokers, but it's a start, a long-awaited one," said a broker.
The OTC market missed two previous deadlines due to poor infrastructure and problems in creating a share registry.
"The OTC system will stimulate the bourse, will help to pull in much needed foreign investment and will give investment funds the opportunities they need," another broker said.

A stock exchange has been operating since last November. Trading, involving 13 stocks, of which only one is privately owned, has been lacklustre in recent months, with turnover seldom topping 50 million lei, compared with early-1996 peaks of 1.5 billion. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
